review.summary: Single-hunk change in src/SDiagonal.jl replacing the `size(::Type{<:SDiagonal{N}})` methods (dispatch on a subtype of a type alias whose parameter sits in a covariant/UnionAll position) with explicit methods on `SDiagonal{N}` and `SDiagonal{N,T}`. This is the classic Julia pattern for fixing a static-parameter that cannot be resolved through `Type{<:Alias{N}}`, i.e. a broken/erroring `size` query on an SDiagonal type rather than a new capability. Recorded runtime evidence shows a stable differential across 3 repetitions with the full suite passing post-fix, consistent with a genuine behavioral defect fix.
review.evidence: minimized_production_patch touches only size dispatch signatures in src/SDiagonal.jl; minimization reports globally_minimal=true and all_hunks_necessary=true, so the behavior change is attributable to this one hunk. runtime_evidence.strict_differential=stable_differential over repetitions=3 with fixed_full_suite_passed=true, meaning the trigger fails at the parent commit and passes at the fix commit without collateral breakage. No API surface is added: `size(::Type{...})` already existed for SDiagonal; only the dispatch signatures change so the parameters N (and T) bind correctly.

review.validation_risks: Because the fix narrows dispatch from `<:SDiagonal{N}` to the two concrete alias forms, any downstream type that is a strict subtype of the alias would no longer hit these methods; a trigger test that only exercises `SDiagonal{N}`/`SDiagonal{N,T}` could mask a regression there. Dispatch-resolution behavior for `Type{<:Alias}` is Julia-version sensitive, so the defect may not reproduce on all Julia versions, risking a non-reproducible or version-flaky trigger. Without the trigger script text, there is a chance the differential stems from a method-ambiguity or overwrite warning rather than a value-level failure.
review.suggested_tests: Assert `size(SDiagonal{3,Float64}) == (3,3)` and `size(SDiagonal{3}) == (3,3)` at the type level (these should error or misbehave at the parent commit). Assert the dimension-indexed form: `size(SDiagonal{3,Float64}, 1) == 3`, `size(SDiagonal{3,Float64}, 2) == 3`, `size(SDiagonal{3,Float64}, 3) == 1`, plus the one-parameter variants. Cross-check instance-level consistency: `size(SDiagonal(SVector(1.0,2.0,3.0))) == size(typeof(SDiagonal(SVector(1.0,2.0,3.0))))`. Add a check that `Size(SDiagonal{3,Float64})` / `length` and a downstream operation relying on type-level size (e.g. a matrix multiply or `\` with an SVector) still return correct results and remain allocation-free. Pin the test to run across the CI Julia version matrix to confirm the defect is not version-specific.
